subject: Re: Dedicated capacity performance validation \u0014 ShopWell / latency & throughput SLOs
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Sam Carter <sam.carter@shopwell.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Feb 2026 16:10:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap: Dedicated capacity performance validation  next steps

Hi Sam  thanks again for the time earlier. Quick recap from today's call and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we run the validation:

Summary of your SLOs (as discussed)
- Streaming first-token latency (TTFB): p95 <= 150 ms
- Completion latency (512-token response): p95 <= 700 ms
- Concurrent open streams: 200 (sustained) with 300 burst for short windows
- Sustained throughput target: ~8 rps (~480 rpm) across the deployment
- Burst throughput target: up to 120 rps for 2-3 minutes during peak traffic
- Accuracy/quality baseline: match current internal LLM outputs  we'll use your eval set for regression checks

What Redwood needs to validate
- Representative traffic: synthetic workload from your test harness (we discussed ~5k requests/day for a 48-72h PoP)
- Model variant: you mentioned you prefer the 13B fine-tuned model; we'll test both 13B quantized and 13B fp16 variants
- Streaming enabled: token-by-token streaming must be exercised during the run

Proposed validation plan (high level)
1) Redwood provisions a dedicated cluster in your region (US) sized for conservative concurrency.
2) Run synthetic workload for 48-72h while we capture p50/p95/p99 latencies, tail behavior, GPU utilization, and memory/KV cache hit rates.
3) Joint review: compare measured metrics to target SLOs and iterate on node count / instance type.

Immediate asks from you
- Confirm the eval dataset we should use (or share a short sample)
- Confirm whether we should route 50% of real traffic (if available) or run synthetic-only first
- PO / procurement timeline if you want Redwood to reserve capacity for the validation window

I've attached the SLO requirements doc you shared, and will follow up with Marissa to propose node-type comparisons (A100 / H100 / L40s) and sizing recommendations.

Next meeting: propose we block 30-45 minutes next week for a run plan review + timeline (I'll send a calendar invite once you confirm availability).

Thanks 
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 4 Feb 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Dedicated capacity performance validation  next steps

Thanks Aditya  that aligns with our notes. A few clarifications and asks from our side: 

Clarifications
- TTFB p95 <= 150 ms is our target for the streaming first-byte only (we can be more lenient on per-token small increments but the initial token matters most).
- Completion p95 <= 700 ms for ~512-token responses is critical for UX.
- Concurrency: the 200 sustained is our expected live concurrency during business hours; we can tolerate a 300-concurrency burst for up to 5 minutes.

Requests for validation
1) We'd like Redwood to run a PoP where you route 50% of synthetic traffic plus a small slice (5-10%) of real traffic if that's safer for you. If that's not possible, synthetic-only is fine.
2) We can provide a 5k-request synthetic harness (will attach a sample file). Please ensure streaming path is exercised and we capture first-byte and per-token metrics.
3) Timeline: prefer the validation in the next two weeks  procurement is fast if we provide a short SOW and cost estimate.

I'll loop procurement on the SOW/PO. Please include estimated node counts + expected cost ballpark for A100 vs H100 sizing in the validation plan so procurement can provision budget.

Appreciate it 
Sam Carter
Head of ML Infrastructure | ShopWell

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Dedicated cluster sizing + GPU comparison (A100 / H100 / L40s)  perf plan attached

Hi Sam  following up with a technical sizing recommendation and validation plan. TL;DR: H100 gives the best headroom for sustained concurrent streaming at your targets; A100 is more cost-efficient at lower sustained concurrency.

High-level sizing guidance (estimates for the 13B family, serving token-by-token streaming):
- 4 x H100 (80GB) nodes  expected performance:
  - TTFB p95: ~110-140 ms
  - Completion p95 (512 tokens): ~550-700 ms depending on quantization
  - Sustained concurrent streams supported (estimated): 200-300 with headroom for bursts
  - Estimated GPU utilization: 60-80% at target load (good for steady-state SLOs)
  - Notes: H100 advantages on NVL/attention kernels and larger cache margins reduce tail latency

- 6 x A100 (80GB) nodes  expected performance:
  - TTFB p95: ~140-180 ms
  - Completion p95 (512 tokens): ~650-900 ms
  - Sustained concurrent streams supported: ~150-220
  - Notes: More nodes required to hit concurrency; can be cheaper if committed reserved pricing available

- 4 x L40s (L40S 48GB)  expected performance:
  - TTFB p95: ~130-170 ms
  - Completion p95: ~600-800 ms
  - Sustained concurrent streams: ~160-240 depending on quantization profile

Recommended validation configuration (initial PoP)
1) Start with 4 x H100 nodes for a 72h test. Run synthetic harness at 50-75% of expected live traffic, plus optional 5-10% real traffic if ShopWell prefers.
2) Collect: first-byte latency histogram, per-token latency distributions, completion latency, GPUutil, CPU, network egress, KV cache hit/miss, and per-request token counts.
3) If H100 meets SLOs with margins, run a cost sensitivity test with 6x A100 to compare unit economics. We'll capture delta in tokens/sec per GPU and expected monthly committed cost.

Validation logistics and deliverables
- Redwood will provide an instrumentation report (raw metrics + aggregated histograms), a short runbook for how we executed the test, and a recommendation doc with expected steady-state node counts for production reserving.
- I'll attach a short perf_validation_plan.md and expected_metrics.csv you can review.

Next steps
- Aditya: confirm dates with Sam for the 72h PoP.
- Sam: share the synthetic harness sample and confirm whether you want real traffic included.
- Rafael: I'll loop you in on any kernel/quantization tweaks during the PoP.

Thanks 
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
